introduction: The study examined depression and physical activity among employees using an employer-sponsored digital mental health platform. Its three aims were baseline prevalence, baseline links between the two, and change over time.
methodology: Prospective observational study of individuals who recently sought services through an employer-sponsored digital mental health platform, conducted September 2021 to May 2022. Adults aged 18 or older living in the United States; 755 at baseline and 480 in longitudinal analyses. Physical activity was measured with the IPAQ-Short Form, depression with the PHQ-9, and perceived mental health impact with one self-report item. Analyses used R and paired t-tests.
results: 47.3% of the 755 baseline adults were underactive. Men reported more physical activity than women. Women and non-binary adults reported higher PHQ-9 scores than men, a difference the authors call statistically but not clinically significant. Physical activity was negatively correlated with PHQ-9 scores. Among underactive participants, MVPA rose by an average of 60 min per week and PHQ-9 fell by 2.8 points.
discussion: The authors report that participants with elevated depression improved significantly, while nearly all with low baseline symptoms stayed asymptomatic. They suggest digital mental health platforms can support both symptom improvement and maintenance, and that multi-modal support may have reinforced physical activity.
limitations: The authors note the observational design could not determine the temporal sequence of changes or causality, and call for an experimental design. They also flag an unvalidated single-item measure, the PHQ-9 cut-off, unexamined industry differences, missing implementation factors, and limited generalizability. They suggest follow-up of perhaps 6 or 12 months.

introduction.q: we examined levels of depression and physical activity in a real-world sample of employees with access to this digital mental health platform
Investigate changes in physical activity and depression over time to determine the impact of a digital mental health platform offering multi-modal care across several domains of health

methodology.q: This investigation was a prospective, observational study of individuals who recently sought services through an employer-sponsored, multi-modal digital mental health benefits platform
The study was conducted between September 2021 and May 2022.
Eligible participants were 18 years or older, lived in the United States
Baseline analyses were conducted using the sample of 755 adults, while longitudinal analyses were conducted using the sample of 480 adults.
The International Physical Activity Questionnaire—Short Form (IPAQ) (35) measured volume of physical activity
The Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9) (38) assessed the presence and severity of depression symptoms over the past two weeks.
We constructed a single-item self-report measure to assess the perceived impact of one's mental health on their ability to participate in physical activity.
we first used paired t-tests to evaluate changes in MVPA, depression symptoms, and the self-reported impact of mental health on physical activity
We conducted analyses using R, version 4.2.0
